verdict.rationale: The evidence only touches the story indirectly. Serverless autoscales to actual usage, adding resources during spikes and releasing them afterwards, so you don't size for peak (docs-33, docs-46). Self-managed deployment anywhere gives an alternative to vendor-metered pricing, and one user values it as a hedge against price increases (docs-48, comm-20). Community reports that Elastic's SaaS is expensive and that licensing fees eat project margins raise cost concerns but do not show per-request cliffs or unpredictability (comm-12, comm-19). Missing for 10: any documented pricing model (per-GB, per-query or compute units), explicit statements on how costs scale with records and query volume, absence of per-request charges or cost caps, and independent reports of predictable bills at scale.
